subject: Controlled egress interfaces & firewall ownership for private connectors
messages:
From: James Porter <james.porter@acmehealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Private connector — final egress gating questions

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for walking us through the private deployment options yesterday. Before we sign off with our networking team, we need a concise list of the exact outbound endpoints and the operational ownership model. Specifically: 

- A short list of IP ranges / CIDRs we must allow outbound from our VPC to reach the Redwood control plane and runtime when running private connectors.
- Any FQDNs that must be resolvable (and whether they require TLS SNI or mTLS).
- Whether Redwood expects us to NAT egress behind a single static IP (preferred by our security team) or if ephemeral egress is used by the service.
- Who do we contact at Redwood if we see denied egress logs — an ops on-call or a security mailbox?

We'd like the list in a form we can hand to our firewall team; a CSV or short doc with mapping to service (control plane, metrics, artifact fetch) would be ideal.

Can you loop in the folks who own egress policy and ops at Redwood? Thanks — we hope to close this by EOD Thursday.

Thanks,
James Porter
Network Security Lead
Acme Health

--
Attachment: sample-fw-template.xlsx (referenced)

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: James Porter <james.porter@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Aug 2028 10:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Private connector — final egress gating questions

Hi James — looping in Karthik (network/integration) and David (ops) who own the private deployment egress model.

Quick answers up front:
- We can provide a compact CSV listing the IPs/FQDNs grouped by purpose (control plane, runtime pull, telemetry). See attached draft (egress-ip-matrix.csv).
- The control plane requires TLS with SNI; runtime artifact fetch uses TLS (port 443) and is OK with standard public CA certs. We do not require customer-side mTLS to reach Redwood endpoints by default — if your compliance team requires mutual auth we can discuss a custom option.
- For predictable audits and firewall simplicity we recommend NATing outbound traffic behind a small set of static egress IPs that you own. Redwood can also support proxying through an approved outbound proxy; we will accept requests from either a fixed IP or an authenticated proxy.
- Primary ops contact: david.kim@redwood.com. Secondary: infra-oncall@redwood.com.

Karthik / David — see James' asks. Karthik, can you confirm the runtime artifact and model pull FQDNs, and David can you add suggested ACL entries and the handoff process (who signs off on an allowlist change).

Irene
Director, Customer Security
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: egress-ip-matrix.csv (draft list)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, James Porter <james.porter@acmehealth.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Aug 2028 13:22:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Private connector — final egress gating questions

James — adding the technical specifics below. I kept it terse so you can paste into your firewall change request.

1) Static egress IP recommendation (customer-controlled)- Recommended pattern: NAT all outbound connector traffic to a customer-owned static IP pool (2-4 addresses). This simplifies auditing and firewall rules. If you need high availability across AZs, split the pool by AZ and use your NAT gateway HA pattern.

2) Required outbound endpoints (purpose -> host / ips / notes)- Control plane API: api.redwood.com (resolve -> 34.212.88.10, 34.212.88.11). TLS SNI required; destination port 443.- Model artifact CDN: artifacts.redwood-cdn.com (FQDN; we recommend allowing egress to 52.84.10.0/24 for the CDN edge). TLS only; client certs not required.- Metrics/Telemetry: telemetry.redwood.com (43.21.77.5). Outbound allowed to port 443; optional to block if you route telemetry through your proxy.- Container/image registry (if using on-prem runtime): registry.redwood-internal.net (13.59.120.0/25). If you host an internal mirror, provide inbound ACLs to our artifact fetch service.

3) DNS resolution guidance- Make sure your egress DNS path resolves the FQDNs to the above IPs; use DNS over TLS internally if your security team mandates. Because some CDN edges are geolocation-based, allowing the small prefix for artifacts is easier than enumerating every edge IP.

4) Hand-off and escalation- For blocked flows: ops ticket to infra-oncall@redwood.com with packet capture and NATed source IP. If it's time-sensitive (impacting production inference), call Ops on-call (number in SSO runbook).

5) Change window and acceptance testing- After firewall changes, schedule a 30-minute acceptance test with Redwood to validate connections and artifact pulls. We'll run end-to-end probes and verify telemetry ingestion.

David — can you attach the ACL template and add the steps you want followed for allowlist changes?

Thanks,
Karthik
Principal Engineer, Integrations
Redwood Inference

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: James Porter <james.porter@acmehealth.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Aug 2028 14:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Private connector — final egress gating questions

Thanks all — attaching the ACL template and a quick proxy/NAT mapping diagram (proxy-mapping-diagram.pdf). Below is the operational checklist we'll follow once Acme submits the firewall change request: 

- You submit the firewall rule ticket with NATed source IPs and the two CIDR prefixes below.
- We validate connectivity from a staging tenant so you can test without impacting prod.
- Once you confirm artifact downloads succeed, we flip the route for a 30-minute smoke period and monitor logs.
- If any denied events appear, send logs to david.kim@redwood.com and include the ticket ID. We'll provide packet captures if needed.

Minimal ACL entries (copy/paste to your ticket):
allow tcp from 198.51.100.0/29 to 34.212.88.10-34.212.88.11 port 443 comment "Redwood control plane"
allow tcp from 198.51.100.0/29 to 52.84.10.0/24 port 443 comment "Artifact CDN"
allow tcp from 198.51.100.0/29 to 43.21.77.5 port 443 comment "Telemetry endpoint"

Notes:
- If you route egress through a corporate proxy, ensure the proxy preserves the original SNI and supports TLS passthrough to avoid breaking certificate validation.
- For customers who cannot provide static IPs, we support a short-term proxy token and allowlist by proxy auth; that is a higher-effort integration.

Attachments: proxy-mapping-diagram.pdf, egress-ip-matrix.csv

Regards,
David Kim
Senior Site Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
